newsitem.title: TURKEY: First Iraqi oil ship likely in Turk port Saturday.
newsitem.headline: First Iraqi oil ship likely in Turk port Saturday.

text.p: The first tanker to pick up Iraqi oil from Turkey's Mediterranean port of Ceyhan is likely to arrive on Saturday, a Turkish oil official said.
"I have heard the ship is coming on Saturday," an official from the state-owned pipeline company Botas told Reuters by telephone from Ceyhan.
The official said oil was continuing to be pumped from the Iraqi oil city of Kirkuk to Ceyhan under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
"The pumping of oil is continuing as it did yesterday," he said. On Wednesday he said 350,000 bpd was expected to be pumped.

Turkey's state-owned refiner Tupras said on Tuesday it was sending a ship to Ceyhan to load the first oil and on Wednesday said the U.N. had approved its contract with Iraq to buy 75,000 bpd of the first Iraqi crude being sold on world markets in six years.
Tupras declined to comment on Thursday.
